summary:
ALMA is health-monitoring software for astronauts built on one rule: no colour without a contestable rule behind it. Every alarm prints its receipt (the exact rule, the seed that reproduces it, and the hash of the experiment it came from), and every "all clear" states the smallest effect it could have detected. The patient is the person; the habitat is only an input to the body.

Instead of trusting a habitat's manifest, ALMA reconciles each book (air, water, energy...) against conservation of mass: in our simulated habitat it flags a 0.30 kg air leak that a manifest-based detector scores at 0.53 sigma and misses. On the only open astronaut blood data (four Inspiration4 crew) it shows why a personal baseline of three samples cannot see a 24% lymphocyte fall, so it declares what it cannot see before alarming.

A built-in Foundry generates its own hypotheses and tests each once, with a SHA-256 hash sealed beforehand: 16 cards, 10 refuted, all published. Live NASA/NOAA data (the Sun, space weather, the ISS) sit beside a real human anatomy fitted to each fictional crew member. Real and simulated data are labelled on every screen.
details:
WHAT IT DOES. ALMA is health-monitoring software for astronauts organised around receipts. Every alarm prints the exact rule, the seed and the preregistration hash that produced it; every "all clear" declares the smallest effect it could have detected, or says "not enough days". The patient is the person; the habitat is an input to the body (CO2 to headache, noise to sleep, radiation to DNA), never the patient on screen.

HOW IT WORKS. A ledger of nine budgets (air, water, energy, dose, rhythm, load, immunity, conduct, time) is checked against conservation of mass instead of trusting the habitat's manifest: in our simulated habitat a 0.30 kg air leak scores 0.53 sigma against the manifest (missed) but leaves a +0.260 kg residual against the conservation law (alarm). Bodies are moni and CUSUM detectors. A built-inlaboratory, the Foundry, generates hypotheses from a library of published mechanisms, drafts each preregistration, seals it with a SHA-256 hash before running, runs it once and publishes the outcome: 30 acts

sealed, 16 hypothesis cards, 10 refuted. ke successes.

REAL RESULTS. On the only open astronaut blood data (four Inspiration4 crew, NASA OSDR) a personal baseline built from three samples cannot see a median 24% fall in lymphocytes: the detection floor is about +/-70%. ALMA

therefore declares what it cannot see befapplied to a real neutron monitor (cosmicrays) catches 41% of severe geomagnetic storms against 6% by chance, but about 13 hours late: it confirms, it

does not forecast. Short sleep lowers ove by 0.21 sd in a wearable cohort; a pulseeffect we sealed failed to replicate in an independent cohort. All numbers trace to sealed records.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT. Crews far from Earth have communication delays of up to ~22 minutes, no specialist and no population to average over. A monitor that knows its blind spots, never shows an unexplained colour and publishes

its own failures is safer and auditable. arth for remote or isolated work.

WHAT IS REAL. Live NASA/NOAA data (the Sun, GOES particles, space weather, the ISS position), real astronaut

blood counts, real wearable cohorts, a re a labelled simulation anchored to publicNASA planning values. Real and SIMULATED are marked on every screen. We found no open astronaut per-person datasets, so we say so.

TOOLS. Python (Django, PostgreSQL), a pure-Python engine, Next.js/React/Three.js, Blender, BodyParts3D anatomy (CC BY 4.0), Kokoro-82M voice, Puppeteer end-to-end tests (475 unit tests, 36 end-to-end checks). Everything runs offline.

CREATIVITY. A ship that "keeps its own books"; a nine-room interface with a deterministic narrator (no language model at runtime); a Foundry that coins ahuman anatomy fitted to each fictional crew member; hashes anyone can recompute in the browser.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED. No claim of validation on astronauts; negative and inconclusive results published; privacy as a budget (with five people an exact average plus one subtraction names someone); open licences (Apache-2.0 code, third-party attributions in NOTICE)erly03/ALMA
